items.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. We partner across the business to allocate and deploy our resources for the highest impact outcomes. About the Role We are hiring a Strategic Finance Generalist to help drive strategic decisions for OpenAI across a variety of areas, including but not limited to: strategic and commercial transactions, capital markets activities, and partnering with Research, Data, and Corporate Development teams on critical initiatives. This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Our primary objective is to improve productivity, helping teams accelerate sales cycles and deliver more value for our customers. As the sales enablement director, you will be responsible for crafting and defining our ongoing sales enablement strategy — equipping our Account Executives and Sales Development Representatives with the methodology, skills, and content they need to win. items.title: Public Sector Delivery Analyst
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! ROLE OVERVIEW: We're growing our Canadian Public Sector Delivery team and hiring Public Sector Delivery Analysts to help run some of the most consequential AI deployments in the country. You'll work alongside our Engineering Program Managers (EPMs), Technical Leads, and senior leadership to keep large, multi-stakeholder government programs organized, documented, and moving. This is a hands-on delivery role for individuals who want exposure to enterprise AI and high-stakes program delivery while taking pride in making complex programs run smoothly. As a member of our small, senior team, you'll deliver sovereign AI to the Government of Canada, engage directly with clients from day one on a clear path toward leading engagements, and learn how frontier AI products are deployed in real, high-security environments. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: - Drive things to closure. Partner with the EPM and Technical Leads to track actions, dependencies, and blockers across Cohere and client teams making sure nothing slips. - Show up in front of the client. Prepare and coordinate client sessions, capture outcomes, and progressively lead working-level sessions such as use-case and story refinement. - Run the cadence. Own the meeting and reporting rhythm including agendas, scheduling, minutes, and follow-ups so every forum lands on time with clear next steps. - Own the delivery artefacts. Build and maintain the plans, status reports, RAID logs, decision records, use-case registers, and traceability documentation that keep our engagements audit-ready and our clients confident. - Keep the record straight. Maintain a single source of truth for program documentation in our public sector document management environment. QUALIFICATIONS: - 1–4 years of experience in technology or management consulting, professional services, or an in-house technical delivery team. - Delivery discipline. You've run RAID, action, and decision logs, refined user stories, maintained project plans on real projects and kept them accurate and clear. - Client presence. You can lead a working session in front of a client, read the room, and know what to say and what to hold. - Strong written communication. You think through the message before you build the slide. Advanced PowerPoint, Word, and Excel. - Technical fluency. You're comfortable discussing APIs, integrations, environments, testing, and releases. You can talk with engineers and report back accurately. - Follow-through. You close items without a second reminder and know what to escalate and when. - Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance. - Based in the Ottawa area. - University Degree in Business/Commerce, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering or similar preferred. - Nice-to-have: High degree of French language proficiency. WORKING LOCATION: This role is hybrid with the requirement to be based out of Ottawa - note, there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. This role requires eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance and a high degree of French language proficiency is a nice-to-have. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.title: Compensation Lead
items.description: We're hiring a Compensation Lead to build Perplexity's compensation function and own its day-to-day execution. You'll build the programs and processes that support how we hire, recognize, and retain people. You should be comfortable moving between program design and an individual offer, building longer-term structure while keeping today's decisions moving. The goal is a compensation approach that is competitive, financially sound, and clear enough for people to use, without adding unnecessary complexity. WHAT YOU'LL OWN - Build the compensation foundation. Assess existing practices, data, and tools; prioritize the gaps; and develop recommendations on compensation philosophy, market positioning, and cash and equity guidelines. - Develop salary ranges and market benchmarks. Establish a consistent approach to pricing roles across functions and locations. Partner with People and business leaders on job scope and leveling, and explain where market data is useful or incomplete. - Own day-to-day compensation decisions. Be the primary partner for offers, promotions, pay adjustments, and compensation questions. Evaluate recommendations against market data, internal equity, and budget, with clear approval paths for exceptions. - Design and run compensation reviews. Build the calendar, planning models, manager guidance, and approval process. Coordinate with Finance, People Operations, Payroll, and equity partners to carry decisions through to accurate implementation. - Inform leadership decisions. Model the cost and employee impact of proposed changes to salary and equity programs. Present a recommendation and its trade-offs, then own execution once approved. - Identify and address inconsistencies. Assess pay compression and potential inequities across teams, levels, and locations. Partner with People leadership and Legal on appropriate reviews and recommend actions. - Build processes people can use. Establish decision records, recruiter and manager guidance, and clear explanations of compensation programs. Improve recurring workflows so consistent decisions don't depend on individual knowledge or one-off conversations. - Own the data and tools behind the work. Establish reliable compensation records, select and manage benchmarking resources, and improve reporting and quality checks. Use approved automation and AI tools where they help, with appropriate protection for employee information and verification of results. WHAT YOU BRING - Experience building compensation programs: You've established or substantially rebuilt compensation frameworks and processes with limited infrastructure, and stayed accountable for running them after launch. - Technical compensation depth: Hands-on experience with market pricing, salary ranges, cash and equity programs, compensation reviews, and individual pay recommendations. - Strong analytical judgment: You can build and audit models, reconcile imperfect data, and explain your assumptions. You know when a benchmark is a useful comparison and when it misses the role. - Ability to influence decisions: You can turn analysis into a clear recommendation, discuss trade-offs with leadership, and constructively challenge an approach that isn't working. - Independent, hands-on execution: You can set priorities, build a workable process, and manage urgent requests without losing progress on longer-term work. You're comfortable being both the person designing the program and the person checking the data. - Discretion and clear communication: You handle sensitive information carefully and explain compensation decisions in language that recruiters, managers, and employees can understand.

items.title: Data Center Facility Operations Lead - Commissioning & Delivery
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As the Facility Operations Lead for Commissioning & Delivery within the Data Center Infrastructure organization, you will lead the commissioning, turn-up, and delivery of new capacity across Anthropic’s growing fleet of data center infrastructure. You will be accountable for bringing critical mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and control systems from construction through L1–L5 commissioning and handover to operations. As a subject matter expert in data center commissioning and operations, you will develop scalable processes for bringing new capacity online, help manage data center partners & vendors, lead delivery schedules, and maintain close coordination with related disciplines such as design, engineering, construction, and capacity planning. If you are experienced in commissioning and delivering mission critical facilities, are passionate about HPC data centers, & enjoy working in complex, fast-paced environments, we welcome you to apply. Responsibilities: Define the commissioning and delivery strategy for new capacity, including commissioning plans, acceptance criteria, schedule milestones, and reporting methods. Oversee third-party L1–L5 commissioning, turn-up, and handover to operations of facility infrastructure such as switch gear, technology cooling systems, and computer room air handlers. Define expectations and standards to enable third-party commissioning agents, contractors, and operators to succeed in each of the critical facility domains. Create standards for functional and integrated systems testing, minimizing risk, and effectively tracking and resolving deficiencies, excursions, and incidents during turn-up. Develop innovative approaches to accelerate time to capacity and improve equipment availability while minimizing cost and complexity. Enable scale-out of capacity delivery through industry best practices and optimization of bill of materials, logistics, and physical processes. Manage partner relationships and maintain alignment with Anthropic goals. You may be a good fit if you: Have 10+ years of experience in data center commissioning, construction delivery, or facility operations as a manager, engineer, technical lead or related role. Can demonstrate a proven track record commissioning and delivering mission critical capacity on schedule. Are a subject matter expert in L1–L5 commissioning, including commissioning plans, functional and integrated systems testing, and handover to operations. Are experienced in third-party partner relationship management, including commissioning agents, general contractors, and equipment vendors. Bachelor's degree in relevant domain or equivalent practical experience. It's a bonus if you have: 15+ years of experience commissioning or delivering large scale data centers. 5+ Critical Facilities Operations and Maintenance Leadership experience An understanding of AI/ML workloads, including power, cooling, and network connectivity Experience supporting technology cooling solutions such as rear door heat exchangers and/or cooling distribution units Experience managing third-party datacenters such as colo operators and/or contract staffing vendors. Experience turning up liquid-cooled HPC capacity, including developing commissioning plans, creating acceptance criteria, and conducting hand-over reviews The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: We're hiring a Legal Response Specialist on Perplexity's Support team to handle legal and other sensitive tickets. You'll help Legal answer routine requests for information and support Governance, Risk & Compliance, or GRC, on privacy and security requests. You'll review cases, write responses, and follow up until the work is done. Support Engineering owns the routing and safeguards that keep these tickets from being missed, answered by AI, or automatically closed. RESPONSIBILITIES - Monitor designated Support and Legal channels, assess urgency, and route requests for human review. Promptly escalate government, court, law enforcement, and legal-threat requests according to approved procedures. - Respond to routine requests using Legal-approved templates and guidance. Escalate matters requiring legal interpretation or disclosure of user information. - Answer routine requests for information under Legal's guidance. Gather account history and draft responses for matters that need review. - Help GRC process data subject requests and meet deadlines. Follow approved identity-verification and data-handling procedures. - Coordinate security questionnaires and data protection agreements, with Legal and GRC responsible for substantive review and approval. - Track each case through completion, including after handoffs. Record decisions, follow up on deadlines, and confirm the work is done before closing. - Work with Support Engineering to test routing, AI bypass rules, auto-close protections, and alerts. Investigate missed cases and verify fixes. - Keep approved replies and handoff instructions current with Legal and GRC. Arrange backup coverage so cases keep moving when you're out. - Handle other sensitive support escalations. Report backlog, response times, overdue cases, and recurring problems to Support, Legal, and GRC. REQUIREMENTS - 5+ years in support, trust and safety, legal or privacy operations, or compliance, ideally at a technology company. - Experience handling legal, privacy, or law enforcement requests. - Working knowledge of GDPR, CCPA, and data subject requests. - Judgment about when to involve Legal or GRC, and care with confidential and privileged information. - Clear writing, including in sensitive customer conversations. - Ability to manage competing deadlines and follow through without reminders. - Experience improving support processes with technical teams, including automation and AI safeguards. NICE TO HAVE - Experience with Intercom, Decagon, Linear, or Kodex. - Paralegal, privacy, or compliance experience or certification. - Experience with security questionnaires, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA. - Familiarity with AI products or data tools for case reviews.

items.description: About the Team Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives. About the Role We are seeking Engineering Technicians to support the assembly, testing, and prototyping of custom electromechanical actuators for advanced robotic systems. You will build and test hardware from engineering drawings and procedures through inspection, troubleshooting, and rework, partnering closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, and test engineers. These roles focus on hands-on work with precision electromechanical hardware, including stator prototypes, motor and actuator assemblies, and mechanical and electrical testing. You will help turn engineering designs into validated hardware while improving build records, work instructions, and repeatable assembly and test practices for future robotic platforms. This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week. In this role, you will: Each opening focuses on actuator builds, testing, or stator prototyping, with responsibilities aligned to the selected specialty. - Actuator builds: assemble subassemblies and complete actuators from drawings, bills of materials, and work instructions, checking fit, orientation, torque, routing, and workmanship. - Testing: set up and run established mechanical and electrical tests, confirm the setup against the procedure, record measurements, and identify unexpected results. - Stator prototyping: support winding, insulation, termination, bonding, inspection, and rework using the selected build process and documented instructions. - Troubleshoot build and test issues with engineers. Isolate problems through inspection and measurement, escalate deviations, and verify the result after approved rework. - Maintain accurate build and test records, part and revision traceability, inspection results, and rework history. - Use bench observations to improve work instructions, fixtures, tooling, and parts organization as prototypes evolve. - Follow safety, ESD, cleanliness, and quality practices, and communicate material shortages, unclear instructions, and other blockers as priorities change. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have hands-on experience building or testing mechanical, electrical, or electromechanical hardware in a lab, prototype shop, or manufacturing environment. - Can work from drawings, bills of materials, wiring diagrams, and procedures, and recognize when the instructions and hardware do not agree. - Use hand tools, torque tools, and measurement equipment carefully, with consistent workmanship and attention to units and acceptance limits. - Troubleshoot methodically, document observations, and know when to pause work and ask for engineering support. - Take ownership of build quality and records while adapting to changing designs and priorities. Preferred Qualifications Experience relevant to the selected specialty may include: - Building or testing actuators, motors, robotics hardware, servos, or other precision electromechanical systems. - Motor manufacturing, especially stator assembly, winding, insulation, termination, bonding, impregnation, or inspection. - Soldering, crimping, connector assembly, harness routing, adhesives, or fixture-assisted assembly. - Mechanical or electrical test setup, instrument checks, measurement capture, and documenting unexpected results. - Inspection, traceability, nonconformance handling, and structured rework. - Hands-on rework, basic machining, or prototype part modification using shop tools. - Use of calipers, micrometers, multimeters, LCR meters, insulation-resistance testers, or torque tools. - Improving prototype or manufacturing work instructions and build processes. items.title: Trust and Safety Program Manager
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized “house,” Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast — both in terms of volume ($21B traded in 2025) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE Trust & Safety protects the platform, keeps our users safe and builds trust with the people we depend on for our growth. This role straddles between program management of Polymarket US, a CFTC-regulated exchange, and on the Polymarket DeFi platform. Every product Polymarket ships reaches traders in a regulated market, so each launch, each user protection and each response to an incident has to hold up with users, regulators and the public. As the function's first Program Manager, reporting to the Global Head of Trust & Safety, you will own those programs end to end: launch readiness for new products, markets and jurisdictions; the controls and evidence behind Polymarket's regulatory commitments; user protections such as self-exclusion, deposit limits and behavioral monitoring; and incident response. You will set how each program runs, partner closely with Product, Engineering, Legal and Compliance, and report to leadership what each program delivers. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own launch readiness for new products, markets and jurisdictions on the exchange and on DeFi: tier every launch, run the go or no-go, and secure written sign-off from Legal, Compliance and Trust & Safety before each major launch - Turn regulatory obligations and commitments into controls, procedures and evidence, and keep the record ready for any regulator inquiry or exam - Bring risk review and user protection requirements into each launch from the first spec, including what the launch can and cannot claim publicly - Launch and monitor user protections such as self-exclusion, deposit limits, behavioral monitoring and trusted-contact tools, and drive them from scoping to adoption - Run DeFi restriction programs, including self-certification and close-only, from flag to enforcement - Lead the program side of Trust & Safety incidents, and build and drill the crisis playbook with Compliance, Customer Experience, Legal and Communications - Take partners and vendors from pilot to contract, with a success measure agreed before each pilot starts - Own the metrics and the cadence: quarterly goals, the weekly Trust & Safety update and business reviews - Build and run Trust & Safety's intake process for partner teams WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 6+ years in program or technical program management, including 3+ in trust and safety, risk, integrity, responsible gaming, fraud or compliance at a regulated platform - You have run a launch risk-review process that product teams used, and can name launches it stopped or changed - You have led or run the program side of a live incident with user harm or regulatory exposure - You have prepared evidence for a regulator, auditor or exam, and turned a regulatory obligation into a control or procedure - You have built a program at a company that had none - You have taken a vendor or partner from pilot to contract - You pull and reconcile your own data (SQL or equivalent) - You write short, dated decision documents with an owner on every line - You are comfortable as the only program person in the function (Plus) CFTC, NFA or exchange experience (Plus) Responsible gaming programs or player protection (Plus) Crypto, DeFi or onchain compliance BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $165,000 to $190,000, plus equity and benefits. This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

items.title: Legal Counsel - US
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. ROLE SUMMARY As Legal Counsel, you’ll be an early member of the Mistral legal team in the US, which forms part of the global legal team. The core of this role is (a) drafting and negotiating commercial agreements to support the growth of our business in North America and (b) supporting the development of AI tools to scale Mistral’s legal operations. As part of a start-up legal team, you’ll need to be nimble enough to quickly ramp up on new areas of law, such as product matters (privacy, marketing, and regulatory compliance), intellectual property, and other matters, as needed. You should be comfortable with charting new paths and interested in designing the legal department of the future. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Draft, review, and negotiate commercial contracts across the business, including customer MSAs and order forms and partnership agreements. - Collaborate with a cross-functional group of Mistral’s technical (including engineering, applied AI, and science), business, and legal teams. - Improve and develop tools to facilitate and automate legal workflows and approval processes, compliance with and creation of company policies, and internal training materials and guides. - Refine and create templates to scale with the company as it grows. - Provide solution-oriented legal, regulatory, and strategic advice and direction to teams across our company, from the initial stages of project development to launch and beyond. - Efficiently manage and work with outside counsel to support projects you manage. - Stay up-to-date and ensure compliance with U.S. and international laws and regulations that apply to AI technologies, including AI-specific regulations, privacy and data protection, competition, consumer protection, payments, and intellectual property. - Build positive relationships across the company and with its external partners. - Occasional travel to Paris headquarters is encouraged. WHO YOU ARE - JD from an accredited law school and member in good standing of a U.S. state bar. - 5+ years of law firm and/or in-house experience, including experience in project management. In-house experience at a technology company and/or in a fast-paced and high-growth environment is a strong plus. - Experience managing technology implementation/solutions projects to meet corporate operational standards. - Experience drafting and negotiating commercial agreements, including creating and refining form agreements. - Fluency in common AI tools, and a track record of responsibly using AI technologies to drive efficiency and process improvement. - Generalist skill set with the willingness to tackle problems outside your core expertise. - Ability to balance an attention to detail with the requirements of a fast-paced company. - Demonstrated business and pragmatic judgment, and the ability to analyze the costs/benefits of proposed resolutions to complex legal and technical problems. - Proven ability to build solid, trusting, and credible relationships, including working closely with science, engineering, business, and marketing teams. - Excellent writing, communication, and people skills. - An understanding of AI technologies and their applications, including how they intersect with relevant areas of law, such as privacy and data protection, competition, and intellectual property, and related ethical considerations such as fairness, transparency, accountability, and bias mitigation - An international mindset and experience is a plus. - Given the rapidly evolving nature of AI technologies and the legal landscape surrounding them, you should be adaptable and willing to continuously learn and update your skills and knowledge. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase . Team/ Role Paragraph: As a Staff Design Researcher on the Platform Design and Research team within the Platform group, you'll set the research vision and practice across the systems, tools, and infrastructure that power Coinbase. This team works across Identity, Payments, Developer Experience, Financial Infrastructure, Compliance, and other foundational areas. You'll define how Platform understands its customers, combining deep research with hands-on design to translate ambiguous problem spaces into clear product opportunities, high-quality deliverables, and shipped solutions. What you’ll do: Define and own the research practice for Platform, setting the vision, strategy, prioritization, and engagement models that connect customer insight to product and design decisions across the organization. Own and run Platform's recurring internal CSAT program, designing surveys, setting cadence, analyzing results, and reporting to leadership to track how internal teams experience Platform tools and surface actionable opportunities. Conduct and lead generative, evaluative, and mixed-methods research with engineers, technical leads, product managers, and end customers, upleveling existing methods and identifying new approaches to address ambiguous research problems across Identity, Payments, Developer Experience, internal tooling, and compliance. Drive process and execution that result in high-quality design deliverables, including polished prototypes, interaction flows, and visual storytelling that set the standard and bar for your product area. Partner with senior product, design, and engineering leaders as a cross-functional lead in all stages of strategy planning, influencing roadmaps and investment decisions through evidence-based research and well-crafted design presentations. Drive improvements in design consistency and integrity across your product area, contributing to existing design systems and creating new solutions when needed, while building research repositories and frameworks that scale research impact across the broader Design and Research organization. Coach and mentor designers and product partners on both research rigor and design craft, raising the quality bar and expanding capacity beyond the core team. Required Skills and Experience: 10+ years of professional experience in user research and product design, including setting research vision and leading research for complex, technical, or platform-scale products and systems. Demonstrated ability to operate at a strategic level, shaping product direction and influencing senior cross-functional and executive stakeholders through research-driven insights and compelling design presentations. Expert-level proficiency in design and prototyping tools (Figma or equivalent), with the ability to produce polished, high-quality deliverables that communicate customer experience and product direction to leadership. Strong command of qualitative research methods, with proven judgment about which methods fit which questions, and demonstrated ability to uplevel methods and introduce new approaches to solve ambiguous problems. Track record of building research practices, operating models, or measurement programs (such as recurring CSAT or voice-of-customer programs) that scaled impact beyond a single team, and driving design system adoption and contribution across a product area. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.title: Senior Commercial Counsel, Enterprise
items.description: Perplexity is looking for a senior commercial attorney to join our Legal team. We are looking for an independent, business-practical yet diligent-minded professional who can carry live deals, extend the infrastructure we have already built, and hold the line on the terms that matter as deal volume, complexity, and regulatory surface all grow. You will negotiate directly with large enterprise customers across a large variety of industries including financial services, healthcare, government, and other regulated industries, partner daily with Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, Security, Privacy, Product, and Finance, and advise on the legal questions that come with agentic, retrieval, and API products deployed inside enterprise environments. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who is genuinely a self starter. This role is for you if you get energy from ambiguous, first‑of‑their‑kind problems and enjoy designing repeatable approaches that scale. You default to enabling the business, frame risk in practical terms, and focus on durable structures rather than one‑off fixes. RESPONSIBILITIES - Independently lead end-to-end drafting, review, and negotiation of Enterprise customer agreements across our suite of offerings: Enterprise Pro, Enterprise Max, Computer, and API product lines, including MSAs, order forms, SaaS and API terms, DPAs, BAAs, security exhibits, customer-paper redlines, product-specific addenda, and public-sector vehicles such as GSA MAS orders and federal RFP responses. - Serve as a trusted legal partner to Enterprise Sales, Partnerships, Deal Desk, and Customer Success, providing fast, practical, business-aligned counsel that accelerates deal velocity, protects the terms that matter, and scales as the Sales organization grows. - Extend and maintain the existing Enterprise negotiation playbook, DPA and Privacy Notice architecture, product-specific term libraries, and fallback positions as our product surface, customer mix, and regulatory environment evolve, so that positions compound into reusable precedent rather than being re-litigated deal by deal. - Advise on AI-specific contract terms for enterprise deployments, including bespoke data postures; negotiate output ownership and liability, agentic-feature risk allocation and translate product operations into enterprise contract commitments. - Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Security, Privacy, Finance, and Compliance to surface and address legal risk early, particularly on customer-data flows, enterprise integrations, model routing, and customer-specific compliance requirements. - Monitor the evolving regulatory landscape for enterprise AI, data protection, and public-sector procurement (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, DORA, EU AI Act, sector-specific frameworks) and translate emerging requirements into practical contractual positions and updated playbook guidance. - Represent Perplexity Legal externally on customer negotiation calls with counterparty counsel at sophisticated enterprises. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR - Exceptional communicator who owns deadlines, proactively manages internal and external expectations, and escalates early and clearly to protect deal timelines and momentum. - A proactive problem‑solver who defaults to “yes, and” when engaging with internal stakeholders: you look for ways to make deals work, frame risk clearly, and design long‑term, scalable solutions. - A disciplined drafter who favors surgical, minimal‑footprint edits over wholesale rewrites, grounds positions in documented rationale, and preserves material legal meaning and risk allocation under time pressure. - Someone who can articulate complex legal risk and concepts in the form of simple, actionable terms for non‑legal stakeholders, leads with practical “how to make this work” advice, and designs creative, long‑term solutions to novel, cutting‑edge challenges. - Someone genuinely excited by novel, cutting‑edge challenges in AI products and the commercial and regulatory questions they surface, and who enjoys turning ambiguity into clear, reusable approaches. QUALIFICATIONS - JD and in good standing with an active U.S. state bar membership. - At least 7+ years of combined law firm and in-house experience, with a substantial in-house component, and a demonstrated track record of independently owning complex enterprise SaaS or API deals from the vendor side, including work with regulated-industry customers (financial services, healthcare, or government). - Experience advising on commercial terms and pricing structures for high‑growth SaaS/API businesses, including usage‑based and tiered pricing, pilots, and expansion frameworks. - Familiarity with data protection and security frameworks (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, DORA, EU AI Act) and hands-on experience negotiating DPAs. - Strong business acumen and the ability to partner effectively with Sales, Deal Desk, Product, Security, and executive stakeholders on live deals under time pressure. - Proven ability to triage and progress multiple concurrent deals under tight timelines while maintaining rigorous diligence, clear risk assessment, and high‑quality documentation. - Demonstrated ability to build and extend durable legal infrastructure — playbooks, templates, precedent repositories, or self-serve tools. - Ability to communicate clearly with business and technical audiences and to translate legal concepts into usable guidance for non-lawyers, including Sales and Deal Desk. - Hands-on, can-do approach to tackle projects large and small, low-ego approach to working closely with the Director and across the organization, and judgment about when to escalate and when to close. - Positive collaborative attitude, comfort with ambiguity and a fast pace, high level of integrity, and intellectual curiosity about AI technology. NICE TO HAVE - Prior experience with public-sector contracting or with on-prem deployment structures. - Experience with AI-native contracting questions related to agentic products - Experience with contracting with regulated entities (financial institutions or health care), especially in the EU/UK.

items.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Customer Care Product team’s mission is to build the product experiences, automation, and human-assisted touchpoints that support our customers at every stage of their financial journey. We design the client-facing tools, scheduling flows, and expert consultation routing that power our new premium financial offerings. Our team operates at a fast pace, collaborating closely with central marketing, the Concierge team, and growth marketing to deliver a seamless customer experience. We prioritize ethical execution and compliance while striving to democratize premium services for our users. As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you will lead the GTM strategy and prospect acquisition for our new premium financial offering. In this role, you will design and stand up a B2B-hybrid marketing motion to bring in prospects who are not yet Robinhood customers. You will personally build and execute outbound channels like LinkedIn, email, and outreach, while directing central marketing and Concierge teams for other channels. By implementing a CRM-integrated martech stack, you will orchestrate conversion paths and build marketing attribution to optimize CAC:LTV. This is an exciting opportunity to build a high-priority marketing infrastructure from scratch and make a major business impact! This role is based in our New York, NY office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Net-new prospect funnel: Personally build and run outbound marketing—including LinkedIn, email, and outreach—to reach a high-net-worth and mass-affluent audience outside our current customer base. Conversion path orchestration: Own both the free expert consultation and self-serve signup paths. Partner with product to lead qualification and routing to expert calendars, nurture no-shows and not-yet-ready leads, and test outreach channels. Channel orchestration via central marketing and Concierge: Set the strategy and brief execution for paid, brand creative, events, and owned/lifecycle channels through the central marketing and Concierge teams. Marketing stack build-out: Implement the marketing technology required to run marketing for this audience, integrating with a CRM (e.g., Salesforce). Launch readiness: Drive marketing execution against a confidential internal timeline. GTM partnership across departments: Partner with central marketing, Concierge, growth, product, and legal/compliance as strategy and budget finalize—understanding project timelines and key marketing outputs, triaging problems in real time, and advocating for the prospective client's needs. Unit-economics ownership: Build and iterate marketing attribution and efficiency, with a primary focus on net-new client acquisition costs relative to lifetime value (CAC:LTV). What you bring 6+ years of experience in B2B or B2B2C demand generation or growth marketing, with hands-on experience building, not just running, campaigns inside an existing stack. Experience creating a marketing stack that pairs outbound channels (LinkedIn, email, outreach) with a live "book a call/demo" conversion flow (marketing automation, lead routing, scheduling, and attribution). Experience marketing a sales-assisted product (such as wealth management, fintech, insurance, or B2B SaaS with a human handoff) where the funnel leads to a live conversation rather than a self-serve signup. Routine use of AI across your marketing workflow, with comfort directing a hybrid workflow of human collaborators and AI tools. Experience shipping outbound campaigns end-to-end, pairing creative assets and messaging with distribution channels, and experience directing other teams or agencies on channels you do not produce yourself. Nice to have Experience in wealth management, private banking, Registered Investment Advisor (RIA), or a fintech-serving high-net-worth background. Experience with compliance-reviewed marketing in a regulated financial services environment. Experience planning small, high-touch VIP or executive events. Depth in two or more areas of product marketing, growth/demand generation, and content/brand, with the ability to operate across all three. Comfort building and presenting a GTM perspective to senior leaders under an evolving timeline and confidentiality constraints. Experience with referral programs or partner-channel marketing. How We'll Know You're Succeeding Primary measure: Net-new (non-existing-customer) demand generated and converted. Supporting measures: Full-funnel conversion from first impression to new customer. Improved efficiency over time (CAC:LTV). Self-serve and referral-sourced growth, balanced with net-new focus. On-track readiness against internal launch milestones. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. items.title: Director, Talent Social Content
items.description: About Us Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. About the Role Creatives disrupt the internet by bringing social first ideas that will have an impact across platforms and this role isn’t any different. Content that has been done before is boring, but in this role you will develop ideas and content with the biggest fans, athletes, creators and celebrities in the world. This content will live across the Fanatics handles with the purpose of building the fanatics’ relationships, brand and GETTING VIEWS. You are someone who can think on their feet and come up with ideas at all times. It can range from a 30 second shoot where you can create one video all the way to planning our biggest tentpole stunts. You are amazing with high profile talent and figuring out what type of content will make them excited and perform well. This person will think outside the box to connect brand initiatives with social first creativity in mind. You will work with the Original Content, Social Programming and YouTube Teams to engage our audience in the best social first way. items.title: Legal Counsel, Corporate Governance & Regulatory
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! About the role We are looking for a versatile corporate and regulatory lawyer to join Cohere’s Legal team. Reporting to our Senior Governance Counsel, this role will support a global portfolio of corporate governance, entity and intercompany matters, together with cross-border regulatory, trade and compliance workstreams. This role is designed for a lawyer with a strong corporate foundation who has also developed meaningful regulatory and trade experience. You should be comfortable moving between different types of legal work including: - supporting global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, intercompany arrangements and delegated authorities; - supporting cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment and national-security reviews, regulatory diligence and filing coordination; - helping the business navigate export-control, sanctions and related compliance requirements; and - supporting legal and regulatory issues arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements come into play. You will work closely with colleagues across Legal, Finance, Tax, People, Security, Government Affairs and commercial teams, as well as with specialist external counsel in multiple jurisdictions. The role requires sound judgment, curiosity and the ability to take ownership of a workstream, identify when specialist advice is needed, and turn that advice into practical action. What you’ll do - Support Cohere’s global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, board and shareholder matters, corporate approvals, delegated authorities, signing frameworks and ongoing entity maintenance. - Support Cohere’s intercompany legal architecture, including intercompany agreements and other cross-border operating arrangements, working closely with Finance, Tax, People and local counsel to ensure Cohere’s entities are structured and operated appropriately across jurisdictions. - Support cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, regulatory diligence, filing coordination and the implementation of regulatory commitments arising in connection with acquisitions, investments, restructurings and other significant matters. - Support Cohere’s export-control, sanctions and related compliance matters, including coordinating specialist external advice and translating regulatory requirements into practical internal guidance, controls and documentation. - Support legal and regulatory workstreams arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements need to be understood and operationalised. - Coordinate internal stakeholders and external counsel across jurisdictions, ensuring that legal and regulatory workstreams are appropriately scoped, progressed and implemented. - Take ownership of matters within the role’s remit and help develop practical, scalable approaches as Cohere’s international footprint grows. What we’re looking for - A qualified lawyer with approximately 4–8 years of relevant experience, gained at a leading law firm, a sophisticated in-house legal team, or preferably a combination of both. - A strong corporate and cross-border legal foundation, with experience across areas such as subsidiary governance, entity structuring and reorganisations, intercompany arrangements, delegated authorities, corporate approvals and other aspects of international corporate practice. - Meaningful exposure to cross-border regulatory matters, particularly foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, export controls, sanctions, international trade or related corporate compliance issues. Deep specialism in any one of these areas is not required. - Experience working across multiple jurisdictions, including coordinating local and specialist external counsel and bringing different legal, regulatory and business inputs together into a coherent internal position. - Strong judgment, range and commercial awareness, with the ability to get quickly up to speed on unfamiliar issues, identify what matters most and distinguish issues that can be handled internally from those requiring specialist advice. - The ability to take ownership of an internal legal workstream, ask the right questions of specialist counsel, digest complex advice and translate it into clear, practical next steps for the business. - Clear and practical communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across Legal, Finance, Tax, People, Security, Government Affairs and commercial teams. - A collaborative and pragmatic approach, with comfort moving between different subject areas and working across functions, jurisdictions and time zones. - Experience in technology, AI or another regulated industry would be helpful, but is not essential. - Exposure to public-sector, government-facing or regulated-market matters is a plus but is not a prerequisite. Nice to have - Experience in technology, AI, cloud or infrastructure, or another regulated industry. - Experience supporting a multinational organisation with a growing international entity footprint, particularly where legal, tax, finance and operational considerations intersect. - Exposure to public-sector, government-facing or regulated-market matters, including procurement, digital sovereignty, security, accreditation or related market-access requirements. - Familiarity with North American, UK or EU regulatory frameworks relevant to cross-border technology businesses. What success looks like - You can move comfortably between corporate and regulatory matters, identify the core issue quickly and make progress even where the work does not fit neatly into a single legal category. - You can take ownership of a complex cross-border workstream, bring together the right internal stakeholders and external advisers, and drive it through to a practical outcome. - You know when specialist advice is needed, can frame the right questions for external counsel, and can turn complex advice into clear, actionable guidance for the business. - You become a trusted execution partner across Cohere’s corporate governance and regulatory portfolio, taking meaningful ownership of workstreams and creating capacity for more strategic, cross-functional and government-facing work at the senior level. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. items.description: About the team The Applied AI Engineering team is responsible for ensuring the safe and effective deployment of generative AI applications for developers and enterprises. We act as a trusted advisor and thought partner for our API customers, working to build an effective backlog of frontier AI use cases for their industry and drive them to production through strong technical guidance. You’ll partner directly with experienced product and engineering teams to turn frontier model capabilities into new features and agentic experiences. The work combines rapid experimentation with the demands of established products: complex systems, real users, and high expectations for quality and performance. Lessons from these deployments inform OpenAI’s product and research teams. About the role You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact – not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve. This role is based in our São Paulo, Brazil office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. This includes occasional travel. You’ll thrive in this role if you: - Bring 8+ years of deep, hands-on technical experience and an eagerness to work closely with customers. items.title: GTM Recruiter
items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy. - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE ElevenLabs is building one of the world's fastest-growing AI companies - and we're looking for a GTM Recruiter to partner with our Revenue org. You'll run full-cycle recruiting across our high volumes roles, partnering with leaders across our Sales Development, Corporate, Mid-Market, and Partnerships team to hire world class talent. This isn't a conventional recruiting role. You'll work alongside GTM leaders to shape role strategy, design world class candidate experiences, and close exceptional talent across North America. You know what great looks like in a Revenue org - whether from building GTM teams at exceptional tech companies or from your own experience exceeding hiring goals.
